title: Life Goal Perspective: Employment - Intervention to improve self-control in rehabilitation patients with cannabis dependence (LEICa)
summary:
Our research project - Life Goal Perspective: Employment - Intervention to Improve Self-Regulation in Rehabilitants with Cannabis Dependence (LEICa) - focuses on improving the treatment of patients with cannabis addiction.

Related patients are currently being prepared for an abstinent lifestyle as part of a 22-week rehabilitation program. Other studies have shown that patients with addiction disorders related to illegal drugs often have significant difficulties in effective self-regulation and dealing with negative life events, which in these cases is associated with an increased risk of relapse and problems coping with life, such as maintaining employment.

The LEICa research project therefore aims to specifically and systematically reflect on deficits in self-regulation in dealing with negative life events through 10-unit intervention cycles using helpful terminology and address these deficits through exercises based on practical examples. In addition to an abstinent lifestyle, the goal of our intervention is to develop a positive attitude toward gainful employment for the purpose of a meaningful lifestyle.

The Alte Flugschule specialist clinic in Großrückerswalde and the Rusteberg specialist clinic in Marth have been selected as cooperation partners. The project is scheduled to run for two years and end in December 2026. The project is funded by the Deutsche Rentenversicherung Mitteldeutschland.
